items.topic: Handling duplicate title in metadata card
items.context: The initiative title currently appears twice: once in the DetailPageHeader (shared across all detail pages) and again inside the metadata card body with a Target icon. Other detail pages (Backlog, Scenario, Execution) do NOT repeat the title inside the body — they use the header as the sole title location. Removing the duplicate aligns with the cross-page pattern.

options.label: Remove title row from metadata card body
options.rationale: Matches all other detail pages. Reduces redundancy. The Target icon could move to the header's entity-type badge area if desired.

options.label: Keep both but differentiate styling
options.rationale: Keep the body title as a larger hero-style heading and reduce the header title. Adds visual weight to the page but diverges from established pattern.

items.context: Currently, 'Files' has a FolderOpen icon in its header, but 'Progress' and 'Items' have no icons. Other detail pages use icons consistently across all section headers (Settings2 for settings, Terminal for commands, etc.). Adding icons to all section headers would improve scannability and visual consistency.

options.label: Add icons to all section headers
options.rationale: Progress gets a BarChart3 or TrendingUp icon, Items gets a Layers or List icon. Consistent with Files having FolderOpen. Matches patterns in Scenario and Execution pages.

options.label: Remove icon from Files header to match others
options.rationale: Simpler approach — all headers become text-only. But loses the visual richness other detail pages have.

items.context: Member item chips show the item title with status-based coloring, but there's no visual distinction between item kinds (fix, execute, idea, chore). In the backlog list view, kind badges are visible. Adding a small kind indicator to chips would help users quickly identify item types without clicking.

options.label: Prefix chip with kind emoji/icon
options.rationale: Add a small Lucide icon before the title text (Wrench for fix, Play for execute, Lightbulb for idea, CheckSquare for chore). Clear visual signal without text overhead.

options.label: Add kind as text prefix
options.rationale: Prefix with abbreviated kind text like '[fix]' or '[exec]'. Simple but adds visual noise and uses more horizontal space.

options.label: Keep as-is — status color is sufficient
options.rationale: Users can click chips to see kind. Less visual clutter. But harder to scan at a glance.

items.topic: Empty state treatment when initiative has no items or files
items.context: If an initiative has zero member items and zero files, the page shows only the metadata card — no guidance or messaging. Other detail pages provide empty-state components with contextual messages (e.g., 'No executions yet'). Adding empty states improves clarity for new or empty initiatives.

options.label: Add contextual empty states for both sections
options.rationale: Show a muted message like 'No items assigned to this initiative yet' with a subtle icon. Same pattern for files. Matches empty-state patterns elsewhere in the UI.

options.label: Show empty states only for items (skip files)
options.rationale: Items are the core content; files are supplementary. An empty files section might not need messaging since users may not expect files.

items.text: The metadata card timestamps (Created/Updated) use an inline layout while ScenarioDetailsPage and ExecutionDetailsPage use `grid grid-cols-2 gap-3` with label-on-top formatting. Aligning to the grid pattern is a straightforward change that improves visual consistency across all detail pages.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md with problem statement, 4-phase approach (layout cleanup, visual polish, empty states, responsive refinement), scope boundaries, test plan, risks, and acceptance criteria based on code review of InitiativeDetailsPage.tsx and comparison with other detail pages.
